messages.subject: simple colour question
parts:
I've used the following command to plot a large dataset (~40,000
points). The points are evenly distributed into 2 types, hence the
factor command. However, how can I override the default colors? The
reason for this is I would like to adjust the alpha so that if I use
to primary colors, the alpha overlap would make a secondary color.
Because I've already used the colour argument to specify how to factor
the data, I don't know how to use it a second time to override the
default colors.

f+geom_point(aes(colour=factor(edm3$type)),alpha=1/10)

Eric

messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: Re: simple colour question
parts:
Hi Eric,

You can use scale_colour_manual() to manually set the colour for each
level of your factor.
Here's the link to Hadley's website on it:
http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/scale_manual.html
There are also colour scales for gradients and the like which you may
find helpful. Anyway, here is a little example where I change the
colours to blue and red and set the alpha to 1/5.

###################################
# load library
library(ggplot2)

# create some sample data
dat <- data.frame(A = 1:12, B = rep(1:2, each = 6), C = (1:12)^2)

# create base ggplot object
ggplot(data = dat, aes(x = A, y = C, colour = factor(B))) +
## add point geom with alpha set
geom_point(alpha = 1/5) +
## title the legend "Custom Colours" and make the factor level 1 be blue
## and 2 be red
scale_colour_manual("Custom Colours",
value = c("1" = "blue", "2" = "red"))
###################################

HTH,

Josh
